notes.title: Onion's New Groove
notes.content: [p][b]Hello Onions🧅[/b] [/p][p]Sorry the updates have not been as frequent. If its ok with you guys I think an update every other month seems more realistic. Sometimes the wheels of industry turn slowly, but we are marching confidently ahead otherwise! If more frequent updates and communication is something you want more of, you can always join our community Discord, Eric and I are pretty active there and tend to answer questions as soon as they arrive.[/p][p]There's a button on the main menu that'll take you right there in the bottom right corner.[/p][h2]The Great Reconstruction[/h2][p]After making our demo and playtesters playing it for so long, we have been constantly refining systems, controls, and every little inch of the game.[/p][h2]Visual Overhaul[/h2][p]We built all new dev tools to help us make the game way faster![/p][p]A big problem Eric and I noticed early on in development was load times were not very favorable. Filling each level with hundreds of sprites added way too much burden on ram. So we've switched almost entirely to tilesets! Now I can stamp hundreds of bushes and rocks everywhere without added any performance hitches![/p][p]Ok.... but what about actual gameplay? Anything new there?[/p][p]Remember that grapple hook we teased?[/p][p]Well we finally have proper implementation. Were still testing it out and tweaking it to be just right. But there are multiple ways to move with this grapple. You can swing like Spider Man and also Zip to points like Sekiro! 🕷[/p][p]Well be showing off this feature more in the future, so stay tuned! 😜[/p][h2]Movement Overhaul[/h2][p]The movement has been completely reworked to address player feedback.[/p][p]We are adding some more things to help you guys test out the new movement and systems. Eric has built new challenge rooms that can be accessed through the main menu. In those rooms we will test new mechanics and platforming. Also... all times will be recorded and displayed in the games UI, so feel free to post your times in the discord! 😅[/p][h2]THANK YOU ALL SO MUCH![/h2][p]Were still in the early days of development, the road ahead is still long. But we have made so much progress and cant wait to keep pushing this game forward. Its because of all of you that we get to live out our dreams of making this game. Every day is an absolute joy. 🧅[/p][p]ONION ONION ONION ONION ONION[/p][p]- Josh | Tall Order Games[/p]

notes.title: System Overhaul
notes.content:
Hey all, CaperCube here, we've got a doozy of an update this time!

We want to make sure the architecture for this game is as solid as we can make it so we can spend more time making the game instead of hunting down and fixing bugs. We think this refactor will help us do just that!

Now that we're figuring out our process here, I've taken on the task of refactoring our code and cleaning up some of the mess we (mostly me, tbh) have made in our haste. This involved creating new top-level systems, gutting the old systems, and thoughtfully moving / organizing / fixing all the old code into our new structures, which was a delicate process that took 4 solid weeks of focused planning and dev time. In that process, I've fixed quite literally hundreds of bugs, and made most of the logic super simply executable from anywhere in the game.

The result of this work is a game with more functionally independent systems, more flexible and reusable code, and a much cleaner and faster content development pipeline! And that's not even mentioning the new stuff!

I've added a developer panel in-game (accessible by pressing "~"), which GREATLY speeds up testing, debugging, and general development. From this panel (assuming you have dev-mode enabled) you'll be able to do just about anything the game is capable of as well as read through the game's system logs (these are mostly separate from the Godot engine logs, so we can keep track of specific game logic). Sometimes it's faster to click buttons than to type console commands, so I also added a drop-down menu in the developer panel for all the same functions. Clicking these items will execute the given function with its default parameters.

There's a few dev-mode tools I have planned as well that I haven't yet implemented, but one that I [b]have[/b] added is the ability to quickly teleport to any room from the map by clicking on a room's connection arrows. Personally this is saving me a TON of time!

Josh and I have also been working on new rooms, enemies, bosses, items and a ton more. Much of it is still very much in development, so look forward to more new content in the next update!

We really look forward to hearing your feedback and comments!
Have fun!
- Tall Order Games
